First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)]_{z=0}^{z=\pi }\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+0))\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,dx & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy]dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}[-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /2}\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}(-0+1)\,dx \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx & =-2{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =-2(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =-\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
